mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rates and declining unemployment rate indicates a tightening monetary policy coinciding with a strong labor market, which typically leads to reduced corporate profit margins and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the Rank IC for the combined signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns fail in more than 60% of interaction-triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in housing starts relative to the 12-month average signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales, as measured by RSAFS, indicates strong consumer spending which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and industrial production indicates weakening demand and supply chain disruptions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the Rank IC for the combined signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns fail in more than 60% of interaction-triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-labor market recovery phase, a rising payroll employment growth rate signals improving labor conditions that support consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of post-labor market recovery periods when PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
